AuditoryStimulus.description:
The sound: a waveform of the set (src/sounds) at initialLevelDbfs, on rig.yml's speaker nearest the picked azimuth at
initialElevationDeg, or on every rig.yml speaker where the pick is "all".

initialLevelDbfs.description: The stimulus sound (the waveform set as one, OpenRigs.Audio SoundLevel measuring the set)'s level in dBFS RMS: the RMS of the sound over its samples outside silent stretches (runs of exactly-zero samples at least 1 ms long), as the task gives it, before the speaker's equalisation, against full scale (a full-scale sine is -3); mute: no sound. The lab's default -40. The workflow stops at Go if any peak at the highest level a trial can draw would reach -1 dBFS after equalisation. Sounds overlapping on a speaker share its headroom: each buffer's peak is checked, not their mix
initialLevelDbfs.title: InitialLevelDbfs

initialElevationDeg.description: Elevation the sound plays at as the trial starts, in degrees: with the azimuth drawn, it picks rig.yml's nearest speaker
initialElevationDeg.title: InitialElevationDeg

initialAzimuthsDeg.description: Signed azimuths the sound plays at, in degrees, one picked per trial: positive is right, negative left, 0 the centre; it plays on rig.yml's speaker nearest it. "all" plays it on every rig.yml speaker at once (logged auditoryInitialAzimuthDeg NaN with a level). With target auditorySide the picked azimuth's sign is the trial's side, so 0 and "all" are refused. Unused where the level is mute
initialAzimuthsDeg.title: InitialAzimuthsDeg

AuditoryStimulus.title: AuditoryStimulus

Curriculum.description:
The Mouse Curriculum stage these values are, and the task file's only record of the stage: app-rig-control fills it at
launch from the share's curriculum file (K:\config\curricula\<repo>\<task file stem>.conditions.yml), its stage's values written over the task
file's; empty in the repo's task files. Bonsai only records it.

id.description: The stage's id in the curriculum, fixed and hidden: never shown to the experimenter
id.title: Id

code.description: The stage's code in the curriculum, S then two digits then a capital letter (S03A)
code.title: Code

version.description: The stage's version, 4 characters from abcdefghjkmnpqrstuvwxyz23456789 (k7f2)
version.title: Version

path.description: The stage's path in the curriculum, one capital letter (A)
path.title: Path

label.description: The stage's name in the curriculum
label.title: Label

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the curriculum file's text the stage was read from
sha256.title: Sha256

Curriculum.title: Curriculum

LaserEndMode.description: When the laser ends: duration (laserDurationSeconds after the trigger) or stimulusOff (the trial's stimulus off).
LaserEndMode.title: LaserEndMode

enabled.description: Whether this is an optogenetics experiment, Zapit running it: every trial sends it a condition from the conditions file (laser off at 0 mW on laser-off trials: the galvos move and the masking light shows), and the launching app checks Zapit is answering before Go
enabled.title: Enabled

zapitConditionsPath.description: Path to the Zapit conditions file loaded in Zapit. Its top-level stimLocations01, stimLocations02, ... entries are the conditions, numbered 1 to N with no gaps. The launching app keeps a copy beside the task file at Go
zapitConditionsPath.title: ZapitConditionsPath

laserPowerMw.description: Laser power on laser-on trials, in mW, the same for every condition: sent to Zapit with each StartStimulus (overriding the conditions file's power; Zapit's laser calibration turns it into volts) and logged as laserPowerMw (0 on laser-off trials). Required with optogenetics on
laserPowerMw.title: LaserPowerMw

laserOnProbability.description: Probability that a trial after trialsBeforeLaser is a laser-on trial, shared equally by every condition in the conditions file; all other trials are laser-off trials, sent a condition with the laser off
laserOnProbability.title: LaserOnProbability

laserToStimulusSeconds.description: Signed, in seconds: the trigger (the ZapitTrigger line) comes this long before the stimulus; 0 with it; negative after it. The trial's start is the end of the interval less the lead, max(this, 0), once the quiet waits hold, and the stimulus comes the lead after the trial's start in every experiment, optogenetics on or off, so timing never reveals Zapit; the trigger only with optogenetics. Zapit is armed during the interval and adds no time. Refused above itiMinSeconds - 0.2 s (Zapit's reply margin); each task adds its own limits
laserToStimulusSeconds.title: LaserToStimulusSeconds

trialsBeforeLaser.description: Trials at the experiment's start with no laser-on trial among them (each still sends Zapit a condition, at 0 mW); laserOnProbability applies from the next trial
trialsBeforeLaser.title: TrialsBeforeLaser

laserEnd.description: duration: the laser and the masking light stay on laserDurationSeconds from the trigger, whatever the mouse does; stimulusOff: until the trial's stimulus goes off (stimulus.durationSeconds after its onset or stimulus.responseToStimulusOffSeconds after the outcome, whichever comes first; the outcome when the stimulus never came on), at most laserDurationSeconds from the trigger. One for the experiment (a session field)
laserEnd.title: LaserEnd

laserDurationSeconds.description: How long the laser and the masking light stay on, in seconds from the trigger (with laserEnd stimulusOff, the most they stay on). With optogenetics on, at most stimulusToResponseWindowSeconds + responseWindowSeconds (the trial's end: the window always runs in full) + itiMinSeconds - what a Zapit trial outlasts its laser (a scan cycle, the bank's longest ramp-down and a 0.05 s margin, plus rig.yml's zapit.earlyStopLeadSeconds with laserEnd stimulusOff) - 0.2 s: Zapit is armed for the next trial only once this laser's whole trial has played, and arming takes up to 0.2 s before the next trigger (checked against the session's bank at Go; before Go only the ramp-down is known)
laserDurationSeconds.title: LaserDurationSeconds

Optogenetics.title: Optogenetics

Penalty.description:
What a penalised trial costs, by its kind (OpenRigs.Trials Penalties.For): incorrect (a wrong choice, a go/no-go
false alarm, a probe's tails) or noResponse (a miss), each its own full values, nothing inherited. noResponse null:
misses are never penalised, and a task that penalises one refuses it at Go (check_misses). Which trials are penalised,
and of which kind, is the task's.

incorrect.description: What a penalised wrong choice costs (a go/no-go false alarm, a probe's tails)
incorrect.title: Incorrect

noResponse.description: What a penalised miss costs; null: misses are never penalised (refused at Go by a task that penalises one)
noResponse.title: NoResponse

Penalty.title: Penalty

PenaltyCost.description:
What one kind of penalised outcome costs: its timeout (the trial log's penaltyTimeoutSeconds), the penalty sound and
the penalty flash (penaltyFlashBrightness).

timeoutSeconds.description: Timeout after the penalised outcome, in seconds; the next interval starts after it
timeoutSeconds.title: TimeoutSeconds

sound.description: The penalty sound, with the timeout
sound.title: Sound

flash.description: The penalty flash, with the sound; off (brightness 0) by default
flash.title: Flash

PenaltyCost.title: PenaltyCost

PenaltyFlash.description:
The penalty flash (OpenRigs.Vision PlayPenaltyFlash, the same in every task with a projector): the whole projector
field at brightness of full white, flashing at rateHz from the outcome for the penalty sound's length, which must fit in
the kind's timeout (checked at Go against the sound file, OpenRigs.Trials PenaltyFlashRules, the same rules).

brightness.description: Brightness of the flash, 0 to 1 of the projector's full white after gamma correction (1: full white), over the whole field and everything drawn, a stimulus still on included; 0: no flash (as the sound's mute). Logged as penaltyFlashBrightness
brightness.title: Brightness

rateHz.description: Flash rate in Hz: the field is white for the first half of each 1/rateHz cycle and the normal display the other half, from the outcome for the penalty sound's length (refused at Go when longer than timeoutSeconds); at most 30, half the projector's 60 Hz render loop
rateHz.title: RateHz

PenaltyFlash.title: PenaltyFlash

PenaltySound.description:
The lab's penalty sound (OpenRigs.Audio PlayPenaltySound, the same in every task), on rig.yml's speakerArray.penaltySoundChannel alone,
equalised for that speaker, at each penalised trial's levelDbfs.

levelDbfs.description: The penalty sound's level in dBFS RMS: the RMS of the sound over its samples outside silent stretches (runs of exactly-zero samples at least 1 ms long), as the task gives it, before the speaker's equalisation, against full scale (a full-scale sine is -3); mute: no sound. The lab's default -35. The workflow stops at Go if any peak at the highest level a trial can draw would reach -1 dBFS after equalisation. Sounds overlapping on a speaker share its headroom: each buffer's peak is checked, not their mix
levelDbfs.title: LevelDbfs

PenaltySound.title: PenaltySound

RepeatOn.description: When a trial is repeated: never, noResponse (after noResponse) or notCorrect (after incorrect or noResponse).
RepeatOn.title: RepeatOn

Repeats.description: Trial repetition policy, condition fields both: a trial is repeated after the outcome repeatOn names, at most maxRepeats times in a row.

maxRepeats.description: Maximum number of consecutive repeats of the same trial; 0 exactly when repeatOn is never (x-rules)
maxRepeats.title: MaxRepeats

repeatOn.description: never (maxRepeats 0); noResponse: after noResponse; notCorrect: after incorrect or noResponse. A probe (target random or noReward) repeats on noResponse or never (x-rules)

Repeats.title: Repeats

Response.description: Lick-accumulation response rule; thresholdLicks 1 with azimuthShiftPerLickDeg 0 is classic first-lick 2AFC.

thresholdLicks.description: Net lick difference (left minus right, absolute) that makes the choice, its outcome at once (the response window still runs in full); in discriminationGoNoGo, licks at the left spout (the right is not counted)
thresholdLicks.title: ThresholdLicks

azimuthShiftPerLickDeg.description: Degrees the grating's azimuth moves per net lick; 0 keeps the stimulus fixed
azimuthShiftPerLickDeg.title: AzimuthShiftPerLickDeg

Response.title: Response

Reward.description:
Reward delivery (the lab's reward block): the reward size, the large-reward trials and the reward tone, which this
workflow does not play yet (only mute).

sizeUl.description: Reward size, in microlitres, planned into valve pulses from the valve's calibration; at most 20, the most one reward may ask for
sizeUl.title: SizeUl

largeMultiplier.description: Reward size multiplier on large-reward trials, above 1
largeMultiplier.title: LargeMultiplier

largeProbability.description: Probability that a trial is a large-reward trial; 0: none (the only off)
largeProbability.title: LargeProbability

tone.description: The reward tone, with every reward
tone.title: Tone

Reward.title: Reward

RewardTone.description: A task's reward tone, played at each rewarded trial's levelDbfs (OpenRigs.Audio PlayRewardTone): reward.tone.

levelDbfs.description: The reward tone's level in dBFS RMS: the RMS of the sound over its samples outside silent stretches (runs of exactly-zero samples at least 1 ms long), as the task gives it, before the speaker's equalisation, against full scale (a full-scale sine is -3); mute: no sound. The lab's default mute. The workflow stops at Go if any peak at the highest level a trial can draw would reach -1 dBFS after equalisation. Sounds overlapping on a speaker share its headroom: each buffer's peak is checked, not their mix
levelDbfs.title: LevelDbfs

RewardTone.title: RewardTone

Spouts.description: The spouts (the lab's spouts block, open_rigs.core.task Spouts) and this task's single-spout guide.

alwaysIn.description: Always in: every spout the task uses is in for the whole trial and interval; they move only at the SpoutsIn cue, never drawn out, and lead nothing (a negative stimulusToSpoutsInSeconds counts as 0)
alwaysIn.title: AlwaysIn

stimulusToSpoutsInSeconds.description: From stimulus onset to moving the spouts in (the SpoutsIn cue), in seconds, signed like laserToStimulusSeconds: negative, the spouts in that long before the stimulus (the trial starts that much earlier; with rewardConsumptionSeconds at most itiMinSeconds); positive, at most the stimulus to the response window's opening
stimulusToSpoutsInSeconds.title: StimulusToSpoutsInSeconds

rewardConsumptionSeconds.description: From the next interval's start (the outcome plus any timeout) to drawing the spouts out (the SpoutsOut cue), in seconds: time to drink a reward, inside the interval, which it never delays; with any lead of the spouts before the stimulus, at most itiMinSeconds
rewardConsumptionSeconds.title: RewardConsumptionSeconds

singleSpoutProbability.description: Probability that only the target's spout comes in, as a guide, on a scored trial of localization or discriminationLeftRight whose spouts move (alwaysIn false); else both come in. discriminationGoNoGo always uses the left spout alone, and a random-reward probe both (logged as singleSpoutOffered)
singleSpoutProbability.title: SingleSpoutProbability

Spouts.title: Spouts

Stimulus.description:
What the grating and the sound share: from onset, a pulse every 1/rateHz seconds (the sound file's 50 ms pulse, the
grating on for 50 ms) until the stimulus off (the lab's StimulusTiming: durationSeconds after onset, or
responseToStimulusOffSeconds after the response if that comes first), the last pulse cut where it ends.

durationSeconds.description: The longest the stimulus lasts from its onset, in seconds: at most stimulusToResponseWindowSeconds + responseWindowSeconds, the response window's close and the trial's end (the window always runs in full), so it is off before the next trial's stimulus, which comes at the soonest itiMinSeconds after that end. Null: no cap, the stimulus ends only responseToStimulusOffSeconds after the response (both null is refused)
durationSeconds.title: DurationSeconds

responseToStimulusOffSeconds.description: From the response (the outcome; on a miss, the response window's end) to the stimulus off, in seconds, unless the duration ends it first: 0, off at the response; null, the response does not end it (it runs durationSeconds); at most the shortest penalty timeout (0 where a reward can come) plus itiMinSeconds
responseToStimulusOffSeconds.title: ResponseToStimulusOffSeconds

rateHz.description: Pulses a second, of the sound and the grating together, each 50 ms long (AuditoryStimulusSet.PulseSeconds, each sound file's length), so at most 20
rateHz.title: RateHz

Stimulus.title: Stimulus

Target.title: Target

TrialCondition.description:
One kind of trial in the mix: its relative weight, its condition-level values (set) by dotted path and the lists it
pairs; its trialType is derived from its values (x-trial-types, derive_trial_type), never stored. A list in a scalar
field's cell is one value picked per trial; a list field's list (LIST_FIELDS: visualStimulus.initialContrasts, the initial
azimuths), at any level, one entry picked per trial. Paired lists share one picked index per trial.

weight.description: Relative draw weight: each new trial picks a condition with these as relative chances
weight.title: Weight

pairs.description: Groups of paths whose lists (the set's, else the task's) have equal length and share one picked index per trial: audiovisualCoherent pairs visualStimulus.initialAzimuthsDeg [-60, 60] with auditoryStimulus.initialAzimuthsDeg [-90, 90], audiovisualConflict with [90, -90]. Unpaired lists are picked independently
pairs.title: Pairs

set.description: Condition-level values by dotted path, any field but x-session-fields'; the rest are the task's
set.title: Set

TrialCondition.title: TrialCondition

TrialStructure.description:
Timing of each trial, every wait on the Harp clock. The response window always runs in full (the lab's
ResponseWindowAlwaysFull block, fixed true): a choice gives its outcome at once, but the trial ends at the window's end
(trialEndTime), so a trial lasts the same whatever the mouse does. A rewarded trial is its end, then the interval (the
lab's Iti block), the reward drunk from the outcome on (the spouts drawn out spouts.rewardConsumptionSeconds into the
interval); a penalised one its end, its kind's timeout, then the interval; one neither rewarded nor penalised its end,
then the interval (the first trial's: from the experiment folder's creation). The interval runs to this trial's
stimulus; the quiet waits (the lab's LickQuietWait and WheelQuietWait blocks) can only lengthen it. A lick first counts
stimulusToResponseWindowSeconds after stimulus onset, where the response window (the lab's ResponseWindow block)
starts; responseWindowSeconds must be given: no limit is refused.

wheelQuietSeconds.description: Quiet wait: a trial's start needs this long with the wheel still, in seconds, counted from the interval's start: the wheel's distance (forward and back added) over the last wheelQuietSeconds must stay within wheelQuietCm; 0: off (the only off); at most 10 s
wheelQuietSeconds.title: WheelQuietSeconds

wheelQuietCm.description: The most the wheel may move, forward and back added, within the last wheelQuietSeconds before the trial's start, in cm; 0: no movement at all; at most 20 cm
wheelQuietCm.title: WheelQuietCm

lickQuietSeconds.description: Quiet wait: a trial's start needs this long with every spout released, in seconds, counted from the interval's start and restarted by every touch and release; a held contact (a paw or chin on a spout) holds the trial's start until released, so licks for the last reward cannot carry into the next trial; 0: off; at most 10 s. It lengthens the interval only when the mouse licks late in it (quietWaitSeconds)
lickQuietSeconds.title: LickQuietSeconds

responseWindowAlwaysFull.description: Always true, fixed for this task: the response window always runs in full, so a trial lasts the same whatever the mouse does. A choice gives the outcome (reward, spouts, penalty sound and flash) at once, but the trial ends at the window's end (trialEndTime), rewarded or not; the next interval starts then, after a penalised trial's timeout
responseWindowAlwaysFull.title: ResponseWindowAlwaysFull

responseWindowSeconds.description: The response window, in seconds from when a lick first counts (the task says when); with no response by its end the trial is noResponse. Null or left out: no limit (a task may refuse it)
responseWindowSeconds.title: ResponseWindowSeconds

itiMinSeconds.description: Lower bound of the inter-trial interval, drawn uniformly for every trial, in seconds; the quiet waits can only lengthen it (quietWaitSeconds)
itiMinSeconds.title: ItiMinSeconds

itiMaxSeconds.description: Upper bound of the inter-trial interval, in seconds; at least itiMinSeconds
itiMaxSeconds.title: ItiMaxSeconds

stimulusToResponseWindowSeconds.description: From stimulus onset to the response window opening, in seconds; responseWindowSeconds runs from that opening, and licks before it are not counted
stimulusToResponseWindowSeconds.title: StimulusToResponseWindowSeconds

TrialStructure.title: TrialStructure

UclOpenCoenDomeDecisionMakingTaskLogic.description: Task logic definition for the coen-dome-decision-making experiment.
UclOpenCoenDomeDecisionMakingTaskLogic.title: UclOpenCoenDomeDecisionMakingTaskLogic

UclOpenCoenDomeDecisionMakingTaskParamet.description: Task parameters for the coen-dome-decision-making audiovisual tasks: localization and two modality discriminations.

rngSeed.description: Seed of the random number generator for these task parameters
rngSeed.title: RngSeed

curriculum.description: The Mouse Curriculum stage these values are, the only record of the stage, filled by app-rig-control at launch; empty or malformed stops the workflow at Go
curriculum.title: Curriculum

trialConditions.description: The trial mix: each new trial picks one condition at random with the weights as relative chances, independently of every other trial (repeats copy the trial they repeat), then draws as the task's values with the condition's set over them. One whole value: a curriculum stage's conditions replace it; the trialConditionId column is its 0-based index
trialConditions.title: TrialConditions

spouts.description: The spouts: when they come in and go out, whether they are always in, and the single-spout guide

stimulus.description: What the grating and the sound share: their duration, their off after the response, and the pulse rate

autoRewardProbability.description: Probability that a trial is an auto-reward trial (logged as autoReward): its miss is rewarded at the target spout, and is never repeated (neither noResponse nor notCorrect); 0: never, 1: every trial
autoRewardProbability.title: AutoRewardProbability

penalty.description: What a penalised trial costs, by its kind (open_rigs.core.task Penalty): penalty.incorrect after an incorrect choice, and on a random-reward probe after a choice on the coin's tails when penaliseRandomProbes; penalty.noResponse after a miss (a miss on an auto-reward trial is rewarded instead), a random probe's too when penaliseRandomProbes; a noReward probe is never penalised. discriminationGoNoGo penalises only a lick on a noGo trial (a go miss and a no-reward probe have neither), so its penalty.noResponse is null

penaliseRandomProbes.description: Whether a random-reward probe (target random) is penalised; it affects only random probes (a noReward probe is never rewarded or penalised, a scored trial always is). true: a choice on the coin's tails as an incorrect choice (penalty.incorrect) and a miss not auto-rewarded as penalty.noResponse; false (the default): never, tails goes unrewarded with no timeout, sound or flash, and a miss costs nothing
penaliseRandomProbes.title: PenaliseRandomProbes

taskType.description: localization: the answer is a side, at that side's spout. discriminationGoNoGo: one spout (the left); lick on a go trial, withhold on a noGo trial; a noReward trial is a probe, never rewarded or penalised. discriminationLeftRight: the left spout on a left trial, the right on a right trial. A target random trial (localization, discriminationLeftRight) is a random-reward probe: both spouts in, and a coin drawn with the trial from the seeded stream decides a choice at either: heads rewarded at that spout, tails unrewarded (and penalised as an incorrect choice, a miss as a scored trial's miss, only when penaliseRandomProbes). A target noReward trial (any task type) is a probe with nothing on offer: never rewarded or penalised, and in localization and discriminationLeftRight both spouts in. The targets each allows are x-rules'

target.description: What a trial rewards, set by every trial condition and never by the task: visualSide or auditorySide, the side of the picked grating or sound azimuth; left or right; go (lick) or noGo (withhold); random, a random-reward probe; noReward, a probe with no reward on offer and no penalty
target.title: Target

UclOpenCoenDomeDecisionMakingTaskParamet.title: UclOpenCoenDomeDecisionMakingTaskParameters

x-required-conditions.message: taskType discriminationGoNoGo needs a condition with a weight above 0 that draws target go, or the task has no Go trials

x-rules.message: a probe (target random or noReward) needs repeats.repeatOn never or noResponse, not notCorrect
taskType localization needs target one of visualSide, auditorySide, random, noReward
taskType discriminationGoNoGo needs target one of go, noGo, noReward
taskType discriminationLeftRight needs target one of left, right, random, noReward
visualStimulus.initialContrasts 0 shows no grating, so its azimuths are unread unless target visualSide
auditoryStimulus.initialLevelDbfs mute plays no sound, so its azimuths are unread unless target auditorySide
target auditorySide needs auditory azimuths without 0 or all
taskType discriminationGoNoGo never penalises a miss, so penalty.noResponse must be null

VisualStimulus.description: The grating as each trial starts: its initial contrasts and azimuths (one of each drawn per trial) and its shape.

initialContrasts.description: Candidate grating contrasts as the trial starts, one drawn per trial; 0 shows no grating (a grey screen)
initialContrasts.title: InitialContrasts

initialAzimuthsDeg.description: Signed azimuths the grating starts at, in degrees, one picked per trial: positive is right, negative left, never 0; with target visualSide the picked azimuth's sign is the trial's side. Unused where initialContrasts are all 0
initialAzimuthsDeg.title: InitialAzimuthsDeg

initialElevationDeg.description: Elevation of the grating as the trial starts, in degrees
initialElevationDeg.title: InitialElevationDeg

initialSigmaDeg.description: Sigma of the grating's Gaussian window as the trial starts, in degrees
initialSigmaDeg.title: InitialSigmaDeg

initialOrientationDeg.description: Grating stripe orientation as the trial starts, in degrees; drift direction is orthogonal to it (initialOrientationDeg + 90 degrees)
initialOrientationDeg.title: InitialOrientationDeg

initialSpatialFrequencyCpd.description: Grating spatial frequency as the trial starts, in cycles per degree
initialSpatialFrequencyCpd.title: InitialSpatialFrequencyCpd

initialTemporalFrequencyHz.description: Unsigned grating drift rate as the trial starts, in Hz, drifting orthogonal to initialOrientationDeg (initialOrientationDeg + 90 degrees); 0 is static
initialTemporalFrequencyHz.title: InitialTemporalFrequencyHz

VisualStimulus.title: VisualStimulus
